overall: The AG found the Historical Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the chair's unposted remarks on a member's attendance were unanticipated 48 hours before the meeting, and incivility claims are outside its review.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the commission discussed a member's attendance record at its February 4 meeting without that topic appearing on the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: We are satisfied that the Commission, and Chair Kelly specifically, did not anticipate discussion of Mr. Oliveira’s meeting attendance 48 hours in advance of the meeting, and did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised whether the commission had to notify the member personally that he would be discussed at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to provide notice to an individual that they will be discussed at a meeting unless the public body will discuss the individual in executive session under G.L. c. 30A, § 21(a)(1).

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair's remarks about a member's attendance were disparaging and uncivil.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review such allegations because, even if true, they do not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.
